newsitem.title: IRAQ: Russia offers to repair Iraq power stations - paper.
newsitem.headline: Russia offers to repair Iraq power stations - paper.

text.p: Russia is ready to repair Iraq's power stations, heavily damaged during the 1991 Gulf War, under an oil-for-food deal signed with the United Nations, a government newspaper reported on Wednesday.

"After a meeting with Iraq's industry and minerals minister, the Russian ambassador in Baghdad said that Russian companies were ready to repair Iraqi power stations particularly those set up by the former Soviet firms," al-Jumhouriya newspaper said.

The paper did not say whether Iraq accepted the offer but said: "The Minister Adnan Abdul-Majeed Jassim stressed initially Iraq's willingness to cooperate with Russian firms in order to enhance bilateral ties between the two friendly countries."

Iraq's electricity generating system is operating at about 85 per cent of its pre-Gulf War capacity. Bombing by the U.S.- led alliance that drove Iraq from Kuwait in 1991 destroyed over 92 per cent of Iraq's power stations.

Iraq has been able to maintain power, but with daily cuts all over the country. It has not had the money to pay for spare parts because of U.N. trade sanctions imposed on Iraq for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait. The curbs include a ban on Iraq's oil exports.

Under a deal signed with the United Nations Iraq is allowed to sell $2 billion worth of oil to meed Iraqis' urgent needs. The deal, which starts two weeks ago allocates, part of the oil revnues to cover humanitarian aspects such as electricity.
Six Russian companies were reported this month to be holding talks with Iraqi officials to buy a combined 100,000 barrels a day (bpd) under the deal.
